wrote /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg5.txt: fix(arrays): ksort compared keys with php's VALUE table, not its key rule

`ksort`/`krsort` selected `__rt_php_compare`, which is php's ordering table for VALUES. It calls
two numeric strings equal once they round to the same binary64 — correct for values, wrong for
keys. php orders integer-spelled keys EXACTLY, so `"+9007199254740992"` sorts before
`"+9007199254740993"` even though both are 2^53 as a double; elephc saw one number twice and a
stable sort left them in insertion order.

`__rt_key_compare_regular` already implements php's rule. The origin/main merge emitted it —
